summary: Support optional archive retention and private HTTP tracing on dedicated query nodes
details: Add stopped-node set-query-mode and read-only query-mode commands. History retention and tracing are independent of full/miner role; ordinary nodes retain full GC mode with tracing disabled.

Offer full Explorer support in interactive setup, defaulting to no. Selecting yes writes archive retention and private HTTP tracing together with the initial node configuration; it does not install Explorer or restore pruned history.

Pass the selected policy through Compose to the USDB chain entrypoint. Debug is opt-in on HTTP only, host RPC publication remains loopback-only, EXTRA_ARGS cannot override HTTP or WS policy, and blank namespace lists cannot expose every API.
Preserve node identity, credentials and data paths; migrate compatible legacy gcmode arguments and reject conflicting or duplicate settings.

Archive activation does not restore pruned history or certify historical coverage. Full coverage requires genesis replay or a verified complete archive backup, with the corresponding USDB indexer history.
Document dedicated full-role query servers, colocated Explorer memory reservations and mainnet qualification boundaries. This change does not activate a mainnet network bundle.
operator_actions: Install a paired release containing both the updated node kit and chain image before opting in.

On a new query server, select full Explorer support in usdb-node setup. For an already configured node, stop it and run usdb-node set-query-mode --state-mode archive --tracing on. Start the node and verify upstream history and tracing with Explorer preflight.
For previously pruned nodes, retain the original data and provision a separate complete archive before relying on early historical queries; do not delete existing chain data.
Reserve the actual Explorer container memory budget in the node resource policy before colocating services; keep node RPC ports private.
